tools.description:
Creates a Colab runtime and waits until it's ready.

Creation is slow and quota-limited, so reuse a runtime from `list_runtimes` when you can, and use a new session (`create_session`) rather than a new runtime to isolate state.

Set `runtime.runtimeSpec` to a spec from `list_runtime_specs` that the user is eligible for. Pass a new UUID as `requestId` for each runtime you create. If the call fails with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, the runtime is still being created, and repeating the identical call waits for it instead of creating another.

FAILED_PRECONDITION means the user can't get this runtime now, for example because there's no capacity for the accelerator, their usage quota is used up, or they have too many active runtimes. Try another eligible spec, reuse a runtime, or retry later. On RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (rate limit), nothing was created; retry with exponential backoff.

requestId.description: Optional. A unique identifier for this request. This request is only idempotent if a `request_id` is provided. See [AIP-155](https://google.aip.dev/155) for more details. If provided, the request ID must be in UUID4 format per https://linter.aip.dev/155/request-id-format.

runtime.description: Required. Specifications for the runtime to assign.

runtimeId.description: Optional. A unique identifier for the runtime. If not supplied, a random ID will be generated. If a runtime with the given ID owned by the requesting user already exists, a completed Operation with an [`ALREADY_EXISTS` (code: 6)](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/437254f595a380cd9323111700ce0fcf9d6d2c21/google/rpc/code.proto#L84) error will be returned. See [AIP-133](https://google.aip.dev/133#user-specified-ids) for more details. The ID must conform to [RFC-1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034), specifically: - 1 to 63 characters - Lower-case letters, digits, and hyphens - Start with a letter - End with a letter or digit

tools.description:
Opens a Jupyter kernel session on a runtime (`runtimes/{runtime_id}`) and returns its name (`runtimes/{runtime_id}/sessions/{session_id}`).

`execute_code` calls that target the session share its kernel state (variables, imports). Reuse a session you opened rather than opening another, and close it with `delete_session` when you're done, because each open session holds kernel memory. Opening a session with the ID of an open one returns that session.

Session.description: A Jupyter kernel session on a Colab runtime. Deleting the runtime closes its sessions.

name.description: Identifier. The name of the session. Format: `runtimes/{runtime}/sessions/{session}`.

parent.description: Required. The runtime on which to open the session. Format: `runtimes/{runtime}`.

session.description: Optional. Leave unset. The server ignores it, because a session has no fields to set.

sessionId.description: Optional. The ID of the session, unique within the runtime. If unset, the server generates one. If a session with this ID is already open, it is returned, so retrying with the same ID is safe. 1-63 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and ending with a letter or digit ([AIP-122](https://google.aip.dev/122#resource-id-segments)).

tools.description: Closes a session (`runtimes/{runtime_id}/sessions/{session_id}`), discarding its kernel state and aborting any `execute_code` call running in it. Files it wrote stay on the runtime, and the runtime keeps running.

name.description: Required. The name of the session to close. Format: `runtimes/{runtime}/sessions/{session}`.

tools.description:
Runs Python in a Colab runtime's Jupyter kernel. Returns stdout, stderr, the value of the last expression (`result`), and any exception (`executionError`). Only text is returned, not images or plots. Output over the size limit is truncated and flagged with `outputTruncated`.

Set exactly one target:

- `session` (`runtimes/{runtime_id}/sessions/{session_id}`) runs in that session's kernel, sharing variables and imports with its other calls. The session is created if it doesn't exist. Use this for anything stateful or multi-step.
- `runtime` (`runtimes/{runtime_id}`) runs in a new session, which stays open. The result's `session` names it: reuse it, or close it with `delete_session`.

Calls to one session run one at a time, so parallel calls to it only queue and can time out. For parallel work, use a session per task and close each when it's done.

For code that may run long, pass a new UUID as `executionId` with a `session` target. A call is cut off after 600s with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, but the code keeps running. After that, or if the call fails with UNAVAILABLE, repeat the identical call (same `session` and `executionId`). It reattaches and returns the output and result if the code had started, and otherwise runs it. Prefer this to running code in the background and polling it. Use a new UUID for each new execution, because once the result has been returned the same `executionId` runs the code again. Without an `executionId`, or with a `runtime` target, a timed-out execution can't be reattached, and a retry may run the code twice.

Cancelling a call (`notifications/cancelled`) interrupts whatever the session's kernel is running, which may be another call's code.

NOT_FOUND means the runtime doesn't exist, or has stopped. Find one with `list_runtimes`, and create one only if there's none. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (rate limit) means the code didn't run; retry with exponential backoff.

To move files between your machine and the runtime, use HTTP as described in `get_runtime`, not base64 through this tool, because the bytes fill your context. Files persist on the runtime across sessions.

code.description: Required. The Python source to execute.

executionId.description: Optional. A UUID that makes the execution resumable. Repeating the call with the same `session` and `execution_id` reattaches to the execution and returns its output instead of running the code again. Once the result has been returned, the same `execution_id` runs the code again.

runtime.description: The runtime to execute on, in a new session that stays open. Format: `runtimes/{runtime}`. Only one of this field or session should be set.

session.description: The session to execute in. Format: `runtimes/{runtime}/sessions/{session}`. Only one of this field or runtime should be set.

tools.name: execute_code

Error.description: A Python exception raised during execution.

traceback.description: The formatted traceback, one frame per entry.

value.description: The exception message, e.g. "name 'foo' is not defined".

outputSchema.description: The result of an `ExecuteCode` call, returned as the terminal `structured_content` of the response stream.

executionCount.description: The Jupyter `In[N]` execution count assigned by the kernel. Informational only. Not for addressing executions, for that use `execution_id`.

executionError.description: Populated when the execution raised. Mutually exclusive with a successful completion.

executionId.description: The execution identifier this result is for, echoed from the request. Empty when the request supplied no `execution_id` (such an execution is not resumable). Use it to resume.

outputTruncated.description: Whether the runtime truncated buffered output (size or line caps hit). When true, `stdout`/`stderr` are tail-truncated.

result.description: The `text/plain` representation of the last expression's value, if the execution ended on an expression. Empty otherwise.

session.description: The session the execution ran in. Format: `runtimes/{runtime}/sessions/{session}`.

tools.description:
Deletes a runtime (`runtimes/{runtime_id}`) and everything on it: files, sessions and their state. This can't be undone.

Delete a runtime only when the user asks, or to free up one you created when `create_runtime` fails because the user has too many active runtimes. To reset or isolate state, close a session with `delete_session` instead.

allowMissing.description: Optional. If set to `true`, and the runtime is not found, the request will succeed but no action will be taken on the server.

name.description: Required. The name of the runtime to unassign. Format: `runtimes/{runtime_id}`.

tools.description:
Gets a runtime (`runtimes/{runtime_id}`), including its spec and `connectionInfo`.

To transfer files without passing their bytes through tool calls, send HTTP requests to `connectionInfo.url` with the header `X-Colab-Runtime-Proxy-Token: {connectionInfo.token}`. Paths are absolute without the leading slash, e.g. `content/data.csv` for `/content/data.csv`.

Download: `GET {url}/files/{path}` returns raw bytes and supports `Range`.

Upload: `PUT {url}/api/contents/{path}` with JSON `{"type":"file","format":"base64","content":"..."}`, or `"format":"text"` for text. The parent directory must exist. Create it with `{"type":"directory"}`, one level per request. Keep each request under 50 MB of file data. For larger files, send pieces to the same path with `"chunk": 1`, `2`, and so on, and `"chunk": -1` on the last piece.

The token expires at `connectionInfo.expireTime`, about an hour after it's issued. Call this tool again for a new one. A missing or expired token returns 404.

name.description: Required. The name of the runtime to retrieve. Format: `runtimes/{runtime_id}`.
